solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do be safe, better to be thrown out — after this

indicators.note: letters thrown out of their order are scattered and reassembled in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to play safe and throw something away rather than risk keeping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges DOBESAFEBETTER into the answer; 'to be' is a link and 'after this' defines the label, which tells you when food should be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed label date marks the point after which food should no longer be eaten or kept.

clue.text: Tummy pain after germ reduced in the country

indicators.note: after places the pain word behind the shortened germ word
reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a bug is a germ, as in a stomach bug
colic is abdominal pain, especially in babies

explanation.surface: A stomach upset following an infection picked up out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural, pastoral life is described with this adjective, as things found in the country.

clue.text: Dog displaying larger nippiness

indicators.note: displaying suggests setting out letters in a new show, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog showing an increased tendency to nip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' rearranges LARGERNIPPINESS; the breed is a lively gundog, so the surface sits well.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively gundog breed, used for flushing game, is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Gear up to make exaggerated claim

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top, backwards

parts.note: garb is clothing, as is gear

explanation.surface: Puffing up your kit in order to boast about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GARB round, as this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to make an exaggerated claim about oneself.

clue.text: Search out supporters carrying bishop

indicators.note: carrying means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: feet support the body, so they are supporters
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Hunting down the backers who are propping up a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is the style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret out is to search persistently until something is found, like the hunting animal.

clue.text: Rubbish a right-winger going round

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: Dismissing a conservative politician who keeps doing the rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory describes something rotating, that is turning round on an axis.

clue.text: Drudgery rendered by Spooner's cockeyed Scottish knife

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famous for swapping the starts of words, signals a sound swap

parts.note: wonky means crooked or cockeyed
a dirk is a Highland dagger

explanation.surface: Hard toil produced by a crooked Highland dagger.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of WONKY DIRK and you hear the answer; a dirk is the traditional Scottish dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, tedious routine work is drudgery, the labour a beast of burden would do.

clue.text: Train initially conks absorbing Boris's money — we'll sort things out

indicators.note: absorbing means the following item is taken inside the first
initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: conk and hooter are both British slang for the nose
a Russian name such as Boris suggests the rouble, Russia's currency

explanation.surface: A train breaks down after swallowing a Russian's cash, and the fixers step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts ROUBLES between T (first of 'Train') and HOOTERS. Conk and hooter are British slang for a nose; Boris stands for any Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Problem solvers who identify and fix faults would say they sort things out.

clue.text: Weren't accustomed to student endlessly roistering

indicators.note: roistering is rowdy carousing, so the letters are thrown about
endlessly means the final letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Not used to a student who parties without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last T from STUDENT, and 'roistering' rearranges STUDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The old contraction of used not, meaning did not habitually, is a past habit denied.

clue.text: Pirate of rough appearance picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: coarse means rough and an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A buccaneer noticed for his rugged looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Barbary privateer or sea raider was a pirate.

clue.text: Strings that may be pulled by number of professors

parts.note: ten is a number
dons are university teachers

explanation.surface: Influence exercised by a group of academics pulling strings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests string-pulling for favours; the strings are the body's cords that can be strained.
explanation.definitionFit: These fibrous cords joining muscle to bone are strings in the body that can be pulled or strained.

clue.text: Reinforce military position

definitions.meaning: to put a lining inside a garment strengthens it
a front, as in the front of a battle, or a row of defences

explanation.definitionFit: Lining a coat strengthens it, and soldiers hold a defensive front or trench row.

clue.text: Pamper common people about to live after great achievement

indicators.note: after places the pieces before it behind the achievement word

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement

indicators.note: about means the next item is placed inside the first one

parts.note: the herd is the common mass of people
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Spoiling the masses who have come to life after a grand success.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a cushy, easy time is to pamper them, like a soft mattress.

clue.text: British shower to come up with ideas

parts.note: a heavy shower of rain can be a rainstorm

explanation.surface: A British downpour inspiring creative thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A group session to generate ideas spontaneously is held, as a verb, to come up with them.

clue.text: Call about the woman's fruit

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to cry is to call out
her means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: Shouting about a woman's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red stone fruit is one example of a fruit.

clue.text: Cry of pain to occur beset by unruly child, bully

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the first pieces go inside the child word

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
ow is what you cry when hurt
to be can mean to happen or occur

explanation.surface: A scream from a child surrounded by a naughty kid, a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate with stern looks and threats is to bully someone.

clue.text: Marine mammal a sleuth turned up atop sea (not the first)

indicators.note: atop means the first pieces sit above the next in this down answer
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tec is short for detective, a sleuth

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: the ocean is the sea

explanation.surface: A whale or dolphin found by a detective surfacing over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: TEC is crossword shorthand for a detective; 'atop' works because the answer is written downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales, dolphins and porpoises belong to this order of sea mammals.

clue.text: Carrier for young fish I catch

parts.note: a bass is a fish
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A container for little fish that I land.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded basket cradle is used for carrying a baby, so it is a carrier for the young.

clue.text: Hit for every person dancing

parts.note: to bop is to strike or hit
per means for each

explanation.surface: A blow struck for each dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dances to pop music, especially a teenager, is a dancing person.

clue.text: Composer with undergarment and Pinafore perhaps

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera about a ship, so a ship prefix

explanation.surface: A musician combining underwear with a pinafore dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinafore' looks like a garment beside the bra, but stands for HMS Pinafore, the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, so HMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: Punch drunk in saga about Rocky primarily

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
primarily means only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer staggering about in a story led by Rocky, punch-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges INSAGA to SANGIA, and 'about' puts R (first of 'Rocky') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish wine drink mixed with fruit is a kind of punch.

clue.text: Start to explode

definitions.meaning: to detonate a bomb or firework

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to begin a journey and to detonate a charge.

clue.text: Having gone wrong, paper's head rolls

indicators.note: rolls means the letters tumble over into a new order

explanation.surface: Things have gone wrong at the newspaper and the editor is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' rearranges PAPERSHEAD; the editor losing his job fits the surface's sense of a fiasco.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang says a plan that has failed has gone like the shape of a fruit.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: the soft fine plumage of young birds

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both low in spirits and the soft fluffy feathers of a bird.

clue.text: 'Eadache to cause irritation

definitions.meaning: Cockney for a headache or snag, a hitch said with its H dropped
to make the skin prickle and tingle

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Eadache shows a dropped H, so the snag word loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or hitch with the H dropped, and rough wool prickling skin, both fit the answer.

clue.text: Typical example of Eastern religious book

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern
pi is short for pious, meaning religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A model case of a sacred Eastern text.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect or typical instance of a type embodies it fully.

clue.text: Last longer than unfashionable clothing

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
wear is clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Dated clothes that outlast the newer ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive something in use, enduring beyond it, is to last longer than it.

clue.text: Unwelcome hanger-on in Arabian legend noshed meat loaf rudely

indicators.note: rudely means roughly, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A freeloader from the Arabian Nights who wolfed down meat loaf impolitely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' rearranges NOSHEDMEATLOAF. In the Sinbad tale a man climbs onto Sinbad's shoulders and will not get off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinbad tale's old figure clung to the sailor's shoulders, hence any burdensome person who cannot be shaken off.
